subproblems.title: Fact (O1): evaluation on an orthonormal n-frame is bounded by the Euclidean coefficient norm (reused accepted theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n) and let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P. Then |α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1})| ≤ |α|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm α.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → |α τ| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Fact (O) and its consequence (O1) in the parent proof ("if v = (v_1, …, v_k) is orthonormal then |α(v)| ≤ |α|: extend v to an orthonormal basis; the k! permutations of (1, …, k) already contribute k!α(v)²"). This is the comparator-accepted DAG theorem regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le, reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is self-contained (the Hilbert–Schmidt identity is proved in step 1). Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; Λ^k = Covector (Euclid P) k (continuous alternating k-linear forms); for b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin k → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(k−1)}); |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e∘I)²)^{1/2} (SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean).
1. Hilbert–Schmidt identity (Fact (O) of the parent proof). For every k-covector α on ℝ^P and every orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P, Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = k!·|α|_E². (a) Standard basis: if j is not injective then e∘j has two equal entries and α(e∘j) = 0 because α is alternating; every injective j is uniquely I∘π with I strictly increasing (the increasing enumeration of range j) and π ∈ Perm(Fin k), the map (I, π) ↦ I∘π being injective; α(e∘(I∘π)) = sign(π)·α(e∘I), so α(e∘(I∘π))² = α(e∘I)², and summing over the k! permutations for each I gives Σ_j α(e∘j)² = k!·|α|_E². (b) Basis invariance: put O_{ml} := ⟨e_m, f_l⟩, so f_l = Σ_m O_{ml}e_m and, by Parseval for the orthonormal basis f, Σ_l O_{ml}O_{m'l} = Σ_l ⟨e_m, f_l⟩⟨e_{m'}, f_l⟩ = ⟨e_m, e_{m'}⟩ = δ_{mm'}. By multilinearity α(f∘j) = Σ_{m : Fin k → Fin P} (Π_a O_{m(a)j(a)})·α(e∘m), hence Σ_j α(f∘j)² = Σ_{m,m'} α(e∘m)α(e∘m') Σ_j Π_a O_{m(a)j(a)}O_{m'(a)j(a)} = Σ_{m,m'} α(e∘m)α(e∘m') Π_a (Σ_l O_{m(a)l}O_{m'(a)l}) = Σ_{m,m'} α(e∘m)α(e∘m') Π_a δ_{m(a)m'(a)} = Σ_m α(e∘m)² (the sum over j of a product of functions of the separate coordinates j(a) is the product of the sums), which is k!·|α|_E² by (a).
2. (n ≤ P and an orthonormal basis extending τ.) τ is orthonormal, hence linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so n ≤ finrank ℝ ℝ^P = P. Let ι : Fin n → Fin P, ι(k) := Fin.castLE k (injective). Define v(i) := τ(⟨i, h⟩) if h : i < n and v(i) := 0 otherwise, and s := {i : Fin P | i < n}; v restricted to s is τ composed with the bijection s ≃ Fin n, hence orthonormal, so Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq gives an orthonormal basis f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ ℝ^P with f(i) = v(i) for i ∈ s; in particular f(ι(k)) = τ(k) for every k.
3. (Permuted frames.) For π ∈ Perm(Fin n), f∘(ι∘π) = (f∘ι)∘π = τ∘π and α(τ∘π) = sign(π)·α(τ) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to α.toAlternatingMap), so α(f∘(ι∘π))² = α(τ)².
4. (Comparison.) The map π ↦ ι∘π from Perm(Fin n) to Fin n → Fin P is injective and every term α(f∘j)² is ≥ 0, so n!·α(τ)² = Σ_{π} α(f∘(ι∘π))² ≤ Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E² by step 1 (with k = n); here |Perm(Fin n)| = n!.
5. (Conclusion.) Dividing by n! > 0 gives α(τ)² ≤ |α|_E²; since |α|_E ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E. For n = 0 the argument is the same (τ is empty, n! = 1). ∎
Formalization note: the extension lemma needs Orthonormal ℝ (s.domRestrict v); Parseval is OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner and the product-of-sums step is Fintype.prod_sum.
proof_key_steps: Hilbert–Schmidt identity: Σ_j α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E² for every orthonormal basis f (standard-basis count plus orthogonal invariance).
Extend τ to an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P with f(castLE k) = τ(k).
The n! permuted frames τ∘π contribute n!·α(τ)² ≤ Σ_j α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E², hence |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E.

subproblems.title: Fact (O2): a unit covector attaining 1 on an orthonormal n-frame (reused accepted theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P. Then there is an n-covector β on ℝ^P with |β|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm β = 1 and β(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) = 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → ∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm β = 1 ∧ β τ = 1

This is the comparator-accepted DAG theorem regcomp_exists_covector_eval_orthonormal_eq_one, reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is self-contained. Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; Λ^k = Covector (Euclid P) k (continuous alternating k-linear forms); for b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin k → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(k−1)}); |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e∘I)²)^{1/2} (SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean).
1. (Definition of β.) For u : Fin n → ℝ^P let M(u) be the n×n matrix M(u)_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, u_k⟩ and β(u) := det M(u). Column k of M(u) depends linearly on u_k and the determinant is multilinear and alternating in the columns, so β is an alternating n-linear form on ℝ^P; it is continuous because ℝ^P is finite-dimensional. Hence β ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n.
2. (β(τ) = 1.) By orthonormality ⟨τ_i, τ_k⟩ = δ_{ik} (orthonormal_iff_ite), so M(τ) = 1 and β(τ) = det 1 = 1.
3. Hilbert–Schmidt identity (Fact (O) of the parent proof). For every k-covector α on ℝ^P and every orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P, Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = k!·|α|_E². (a) Standard basis: if j is not injective then e∘j has two equal entries and α(e∘j) = 0 because α is alternating; every injective j is uniquely I∘π with I strictly increasing (the increasing enumeration of range j) and π ∈ Perm(Fin k), the map (I, π) ↦ I∘π being injective; α(e∘(I∘π)) = sign(π)·α(e∘I), so α(e∘(I∘π))² = α(e∘I)², and summing over the k! permutations for each I gives Σ_j α(e∘j)² = k!·|α|_E². (b) Basis invariance: put O_{ml} := ⟨e_m, f_l⟩, so f_l = Σ_m O_{ml}e_m and, by Parseval for the orthonormal basis f, Σ_l O_{ml}O_{m'l} = Σ_l ⟨e_m, f_l⟩⟨e_{m'}, f_l⟩ = ⟨e_m, e_{m'}⟩ = δ_{mm'}. By multilinearity α(f∘j) = Σ_{m : Fin k → Fin P} (Π_a O_{m(a)j(a)})·α(e∘m), hence Σ_j α(f∘j)² = Σ_{m,m'} α(e∘m)α(e∘m') Σ_j Π_a O_{m(a)j(a)}O_{m'(a)j(a)} = Σ_{m,m'} α(e∘m)α(e∘m') Π_a (Σ_l O_{m(a)l}O_{m'(a)l}) = Σ_{m,m'} α(e∘m)α(e∘m') Π_a δ_{m(a)m'(a)} = Σ_m α(e∘m)² (the sum over j of a product of functions of the separate coordinates j(a) is the product of the sums), which is k!·|α|_E² by (a).
4. (n ≤ P and an orthonormal basis extending τ.) τ is orthonormal, hence linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so n ≤ finrank ℝ ℝ^P = P. Let ι : Fin n → Fin P, ι(k) := Fin.castLE k (injective). Define v(i) := τ(⟨i, h⟩) if h : i < n and v(i) := 0 otherwise, and s := {i : Fin P | i < n}; v restricted to s is τ composed with the bijection s ≃ Fin n, hence orthonormal, so Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq gives an orthonormal basis f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ ℝ^P with f(i) = v(i) for i ∈ s; in particular f(ι(k)) = τ(k) for every k.
5. (Values on basis tuples.) Fix j : Fin n → Fin P; since τ_i = f_{ι(i)}, M(f∘j)_{ik} = ⟨f_{ι(i)}, f_{j(k)}⟩ = [ι(i) = j(k)]. (a) If j = ι∘π for some π ∈ Perm(Fin n), then f∘j = τ∘π and β(f∘j) = sign(π)·β(τ) = ±1, so β(f∘j)² = 1. (b) Otherwise β(f∘j) = 0: if some j(k) ∉ range ι, column k of M(f∘j) is zero (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_column_eq_zero); if range j ⊆ range ι, then j = ι∘ρ for a map ρ : Fin n → Fin n that is not a permutation, hence not injective (Finite.injective_iff_bijective), so f∘j has two equal entries and β(f∘j) = 0 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective). (c) π ↦ ι∘π is injective, so exactly n! tuples fall under (a), and Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} β(f∘j)² = n!.
6. (Norm.) By step 3 (k = n, α = β): n! = n!·|β|_E². As n! > 0, |β|_E² = 1, and as |β|_E ≥ 0, |β|_E = 1.
7. (Conclusion.) covectorEuclideanNorm β = 1 (step 6) and β τ = 1 (step 2). ∎

subproblems.title: Hⁿ of a disc in an n-dimensional linear subspace equals ω_nρⁿ (reused accepted theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with dim Q = n (Module.finrank ℝ Q = n), let y ∈ Q and ρ > 0. Then H^n(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n), where H^n = μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P and ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝ^n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P) (ρ : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ Q = n → y ∈ Q → 0 < ρ → μHE[n] ((Q : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball y ρ) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted DAG theorem idtp_tdc_subspace_ball_measure, reused with its byte-identical frozen type; in the parent proof it is the fact "V₀ is isometric to ℝⁿ with Hⁿ⌞V₀ corresponding to Lebesgue measure" (steps 6–8: Hⁿ(V₀ ∩ B_r(u)) = ω_nrⁿ). Its accepted natural proof is reproduced verbatim below; there, "the parent proof" refers to that node's original parent in the dimension-reduction branch:
Source: the conventions of the parent proof ("For a 2-dimensional subspace Q, H²⌞Q is the image of Lebesgue measure of ℝ² under a linear isometry (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so H²(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_2ρ² for y ∈ Q"), proved here in every dimension n.
1. Let ι : Q → ℝ^P be the inclusion x ↦ (x : ℝ^P). It is an isometry, because the norm of Q is the restriction of the norm of ℝ^P, and its range is Q. By Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_preimage, μHE[n](ι⁻¹(B_ρ(y))) = μHE[n](B_ρ(y) ∩ Q), where the left side is the measure μHE[n] of the metric space Q. Also B_ρ(y) ∩ Q = Q ∩ B_ρ(y).
2. Let y₀ := ⟨y, hy⟩ ∈ Q. Since the distance of Q is the restriction of the distance of ℝ^P, ι⁻¹(B_ρ(y)) = B_ρ(y₀), the open ball of Q.
3. Q is a finite-dimensional real inner product space with finrank ℝ Q = n. By Mathlib InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume (μHE[finrank ℝ Q] = volume on Q, the volume of measureSpaceOfInnerProductSpace), rewritten with finrank ℝ Q = n, the measure μHE[n] of Q equals volume.
4. volume on Q is an additive Haar measure, so Mathlib Measure.addHaar_ball_of_pos (ρ > 0) gives volume(B_ρ(y₀)) = ofReal(ρ^{finrank ℝ Q})·volume(B_1(0_Q)) = ofReal(ρ^n)·volume(B_1(0_Q)).
5. Let b be stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q reindexed by Fin n (possible since finrank ℝ Q = n) and e := b.repr : Q ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) = Euclid n. Haar scaling gives volume(B_ρ(y)) = ρ^n·volume(B_1(0_Q)).

subproblems.title: Exterior derivative of a scalar function times a constant covector (reused accepted theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, a : ℝ^P → ℝ, β a fixed m-covector on ℝ^P (β ∈ Covector (Euclid P) m), x ∈ ℝ^P with a differentiable at x, and w = (w₀, …, w_m) ∈ (ℝ^P)^{m+1}. Then the exterior derivative of the m-form y ↦ a(y)·β satisfies d(a·β)(x)(w) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i · (Da(x)wᵢ · β(Fin.removeNth i w)).

Notation: ℝ^p means Euclid p = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p); e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ) is the l-th standard basis vector; for an (m+1)-tuple w, removeNth i w := Fin.removeNth i w is the m-tuple with entry i deleted, so (removeNth i w)(l) = w(i.succAbove l) (Fin.removeNth_apply); Covector E m = E [⋀^Fin m]→L[ℝ] ℝ (continuous alternating m-linear forms); DifferentialForm E m = E → Covector E m; exteriorDerivative = Mathlib's extDeriv (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.exteriorDerivative is an abbrev), with the alternating-sum formula dω(x)(w₀,…,w_m) = Σᵢ (−1)^i • D[y ↦ ω(y)(removeNth i w)](x)(wᵢ) for ω differentiable at x (exteriorDerivative_apply); IsSmoothForm ψ := ContDiff ℝ ∞ ψ where ∞ = ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) (in the frozen contract scope `∞` denotes ENNReal's ∞ because of `open scoped ENNReal`, so write the order as (⊤ : ℕ∞)).
1. The form ω(y) := a(y) • β is differentiable at x, since a is differentiable at x and β is a constant vector of the normed space Covector (Euclid P) m (DifferentiableAt.smul_const).
2. By the alternating-sum expansion of the exterior derivative (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.exteriorDerivative_apply, i.e. Mathlib's extDeriv_apply, applicable by step 1): dω(x)(w) = Σᵢ (−1 : ℤ)^i • D[y ↦ ω(y)(removeNth i w)](x)(wᵢ).

Because (a(y) • β)(removeNth i w) = a(y) · β(removeNth i w) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul), the scalar function y ↦ ω(y)(removeNth i w) equals y ↦ a(y) · c with the constant c := β(removeNth i w). Its derivative at x is the map h ↦ (Da(x)h) · c (fderiv_mul_const, using differentiability of a at x). Evaluating at wᵢ gives (Da(x)wᵢ) · β(removeNth i w).

Each term is the derivative of y ↦ a(y)·β(removeNth i w), which is (Da(x)wᵢ)·β(removeNth i w) by fderiv_mul_const.

subproblems.title: Vanishing directional-derivative integrals force translation invariance of a locally finite measure
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, ν a Borel measure on ℝ^P = Euclid P with ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, and v ∈ ℝ^P. Assume ∫Dφ(y)[v] dν(y) = 0 (the Bochner integral of y ↦ fderiv ℝ φ y v) for every C^∞ function φ : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support. Then ν({x : v + x ∈ A}) = ν(A) for every Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P, i.e. ν is invariant under the translation by v.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (v : Euclid P), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ν K < ∞) → (∀ φ : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → ∫ y, fderiv ℝ φ y v ∂ν = 0) → ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → ν ((fun x => v + x) ⁻¹' A) = ν A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 (V9, translation invariance) of the parent proof, for one vector v (there v = v_α, and the hypothesis is the conclusion ∫Dφ(y)[v_α]dν(y) = 0 of step 1).
Notation: τ(x) := v + x; τ_#ν := Measure.map τ ν, so (τ_#ν)(A) = ν(τ⁻¹(A)) = ν({x : v + x ∈ A}) for Borel A (Measure.map_apply, τ is continuous) and ∫g d(τ_#ν) = ∫g(v + y) dν(y) for continuous g with compact support (integral_map). C_c := continuous real functions on ℝ^P with compact support; vol := Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ^P; ‖·‖_∞ the sup norm.
1. (Integrability.) A continuous function with compact support K is bounded and vanishes off K, and ν(K) < ∞, so it is ν-integrable; the same holds for y ↦ g(v + y), which is supported in the compact set K − v.
2. (Derivative of the translated integral.) Fix a C^∞ function φ with compact support and put F(s) := ∫φ(y + s v) dν(y), s ∈ ℝ. Choose R_φ with tsupport φ ⊆ B̄_{R_φ}(0) and fix s₀ ∈ ℝ. For s ∈ (s₀ − 1, s₀ + 1) the functions y ↦ φ(y + s v) and y ↦ Dφ(y + s v)[v] vanish outside the closed ball K_{s₀} := B̄_{R_φ + (|s₀| + 1)‖v‖}(0) (if y + s v ∈ tsupport φ then ‖y‖ ≤ R_φ + |s|‖v‖) and are bounded by ‖φ‖_∞ and ‖Dφ‖_∞‖v‖ (Dφ is continuous with compact support, so ‖Dφ‖_∞ < ∞). For each y, s ↦ φ(y + s v) has derivative Dφ(y + s v)[v] (chain rule). Since ν(K_{s₀}) < ∞, the function ‖Dφ‖_∞‖v‖·1_{K_{s₀}} is an integrable bound for the s-derivatives, uniformly for s in the neighbourhood (s₀ − 1, s₀ + 1) = ball s₀ 1 of s₀, and y ↦ Dφ(y + s v)[v] is continuous hence measurable; differentiation under the integral sign (hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le, with the neighbourhood ball s₀ 1 ∈ 𝓝 s₀) gives that F is differentiable at s₀ with F'(s₀) = ∫Dφ(y + s₀v)[v] dν(y).
3. (F' = 0.) For fixed s₀, ψ(y) := φ(y + s₀v) is C^∞ with compact support (tsupport ψ = tsupport φ − s₀v) and Dψ(y)[v] = Dφ(y + s₀v)[v] (chain rule for a translation). By the hypothesis applied to ψ, F'(s₀) = ∫Dψ(y)[v] dν(y) = 0. So F is differentiable on ℝ with derivative 0, hence constant (is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero); F(1) = F(0) reads ∫φ(v + y) dν(y) = ∫φ dν for every C^∞ function φ with compact support.
4. (Mollifiers.) For k ≥ 1, exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset (at the point 0 with the neighbourhood B_{1/k}(0), smoothness order ⊤) gives a C^∞ function ψ_k : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with compact support, tsupport ψ_k ⊆ B_{1/k}(0) and ψ_k(0) = 1. c_k := ∫ψ_k dvol > 0 (Continuous.integral_pos_of_hasCompactSupport_nonneg_nonzero), and ρ_k := c_k⁻¹ψ_k satisfies ρ_k ≥ 0, ∫ρ_k dvol = 1, support ρ_k ⊆ B_{1/k}(0), ρ_k C^∞ with compact support.
5. (Smooth approximation of g ∈ C_c.) Let g ∈ C_c, choose R₀ with tsupport g ⊆ B̄_{R₀}(0), put K₁ := B̄_{R₀+1}(0) (compact), and let g_k := ρ_k ⋆ g, g_k(x) = ∫ρ_k(t)g(x − t) dvol(t) (Mathlib convolution with ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ). (a) g_k is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left: ρ_k is C^∞ with compact support and g is locally integrable). (b) g_k(x) ≠ 0 forces x − t ∈ tsupport g for some t ∈ B_{1/k}(0), so ‖x‖ ≤ R₀ + 1: g_k vanishes outside K₁ and has compact support (no pointwise set sums are needed). (c) |g_k(x)| ≤ ∫ρ_k(t)|g(x − t)| dvol(t) ≤ ‖g‖_∞. (d) g_k(x) → g(x) for every x: given ε > 0 choose δ > 0 with |g(x') − g(x)| ≤ ε for |x' − x| < δ (continuity); for 1/k < δ, dist_convolution_le (support ρ_k ⊆ B_{1/k}(0), ρ_k ≥ 0, ∫ρ_k = 1) gives |g_k(x) − g(x)| ≤ ε.
6. (All of C_c.) By step 3 applied to g_k, ∫g_k(v + y) dν(y) = ∫g_k dν for every k. The integrands are dominated by ‖g‖_∞·1_{K₁ ∪ B̄_{R₀+1}(−v)} ({y : v + y ∈ K₁} = B̄_{R₀+1}(−v)), which is ν-integrable (compact set, step 1), and converge pointwise to g(v + y) and g(y) by step 5(d). By dominated convergence, ∫g(v + y) dν(y) = ∫g dν, i.e. ∫g d(τ_#ν) = ∫g dν for all g ∈ C_c.
7. (Uniqueness.) τ_#ν is finite on compact sets: (τ_#ν)(K) = ν(K − v) < ∞ because K − v is compact. ℝ^P is a σ-compact, locally compact metric space, so ν and τ_#ν are locally finite (isLocallyFiniteMeasure_of_isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts) and therefore regular (Measure.Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure). Two regular measures with the same integrals of all compactly supported continuous functions are equal (Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported), so τ_#ν = ν.
8. (Conclusion.) For Borel A: ν({x : v + x ∈ A}) = (τ_#ν)(A) = ν(A). ∎
Formalization note: ContDiffBump.normed and the SmoothApprox density lemmas are not in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission; steps 4–5 use only exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset, Continuous.integral_pos_of_hasCompactSupport_nonneg_nonzero, HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left and dist_convolution_le, all reachable.
proof_key_steps: For φ ∈ C_c^∞, F(s) = ∫φ(y + sv)dν is differentiable with F'(s) = ∫Dφ(y + sv)[v]dν, which is 0 by the hypothesis applied to φ(· + sv); hence ∫φ(v + y)dν = ∫φdν.
Mollify g ∈ C_c: g_k = ρ_k ⋆ g is C^∞, supported in a fixed compact set, bounded by ‖g‖_∞ and g_k → g pointwise; dominated convergence gives ∫g(v + y)dν = ∫g dν.
The translate of ν and ν are locally finite, hence regular, with equal C_c integrals, so they coincide (Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported); evaluate on Borel A.

subproblems.title: The cycle condition gives a subspace V of directional invariances such that ζ₀ kills w^♭∧α for w ⊥ V
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, n := d+1, ν a Borel measure on ℝ^P with ν(K) < ∞ for compact K, and ζ₀ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n, a continuous linear functional on n-covectors). Assume ∫ζ₀(dφ(y))dν(y) = 0 for every test d-form φ on ℝ^P (φ ∈ TestFormOn univ d; d = exteriorDerivative). Then there is a linear subspace V ⊆ ℝ^P such that (a) ∫Dψ(y)[v]dν(y) = 0 for every v ∈ V and every C^∞ function ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support, and (b) ζ₀(γ) = 0 whenever w ∈ V^⊥, α is a d-covector and γ is an n-covector with γ(u_0, …, u_d) = Σ_{i=0}^{d}(−1)^i⟨w, u_i⟩α(u_0, …, û_i, …, u_d) for all u (û_i omitted, i.e. α(Fin.removeNth i u)); such a γ is w^♭∧α.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (ζ₀ : MultiVector P (d + 1)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ν K < ∞) → (∀ φ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d, ∫ y, ζ₀ (exteriorDerivative (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) y) ∂ν = 0) → ∃ V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), (∀ v ∈ V, ∀ φ : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → ∫ y, fderiv ℝ φ y v ∂ν = 0) ∧ ∀ w ∈ Vᗮ, ∀ (α : Covector (Euclid P) d) (γ : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1)), (∀ u : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P, γ u = ∑ i : Fin (d + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * (inner ℝ w (u i) * α (i.removeNth u))) → ζ₀ γ = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0 and 1 (V9) of the parent proof, together with the vanishing used in its step 3 (ζ₀(e'^{i♭}∧α) = ⟨v_α, e'_i⟩ = 0 for e'_i ⊥ V₀). Uses the sibling extderiv_smul (accepted dgcr_bwd_extDeriv_smul_const): for a : ℝ^P → ℝ differentiable at x and a constant m-covector β, exteriorDerivative (y ↦ a(y)•β) x u = Σ_i (−1)^i·(Da(x)(u_i)·β(removeNth i u)).
Notation: n = d + 1; ⟨·,·⟩ the inner product of ℝ^P; for w ∈ ℝ^P and a d-covector α, w^♭∧α := exteriorDerivative (y ↦ ⟨w, y⟩•α) 0, an n-covector.
1. (The wedge w^♭∧α.) a_w(y) := ⟨w, y⟩ is linear and continuous, hence differentiable at every point with Da_w(x)(u) = ⟨w, u⟩. By extderiv_smul (m = d, a = a_w, β = α, x = 0), (w^♭∧α)(u) = Σ_i (−1)^i⟨w, u_i⟩α(removeNth i u) for all u : Fin n → ℝ^P. Consequently: (i) any n-covector γ with γ(u) = Σ_i (−1)^i⟨w, u_i⟩α(removeNth i u) for all u equals w^♭∧α (continuous alternating maps with equal values are equal, ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext); (ii) w^♭∧α is additive and homogeneous in w (read off the formula).
2. (The vectors v_α.) For a fixed d-covector α, ℓ_α(w) := ζ₀(w^♭∧α) is linear in w (step 1(ii), ζ₀ linear), hence a continuous linear functional on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P. Let v_α := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ ℝ^P).symm ℓ_α be its Riesz representative: ⟨v_α, w⟩ = ζ₀(w^♭∧α) for all w (equivalently v_α = Σ_m ζ₀(e_m^♭∧α)e_m in the standard basis). Let V := span{v_α : α a d-covector} (Submodule.span ℝ (range (α ↦ v_α))).
3. (Test forms ψα.) Let ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and α a d-covector. The d-form ω(y) := ψ(y)•α is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul with a constant), has compact support (support ω ⊆ support ψ, HasCompactSupport.smul_right) and tsupport ω ⊆ univ, so ω ∈ TestFormOn univ d.
4. (dω = (∇ψ)^♭∧α.) Fix y and let ∇ψ(y) ∈ ℝ^P be the Riesz representative of Dψ(y), i.e. Dψ(y)(u) = ⟨∇ψ(y), u⟩ for all u. ψ is differentiable at y, so by extderiv_smul (a = ψ) dω(y)(u) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dψ(y)(u_i)α(removeNth i u) = Σ_i (−1)^i⟨∇ψ(y), u_i⟩α(removeNth i u); by step 1(i), dω(y) = (∇ψ(y))^♭∧α. Hence ζ₀(dω(y)) = ⟨v_α, ∇ψ(y)⟩ = ⟨∇ψ(y), v_α⟩ = Dψ(y)[v_α] (symmetry of the real inner product).
5. (Proof of (a).) Let ψ be C^∞ with compact support. (i) For every d-covector α, by step 4 the integrands y ↦ Dψ(y)[v_α] and y ↦ ζ₀(dω(y)) (ω = ψα) agree at every y, so ∫Dψ(y)[v_α]dν(y) = ∫ζ₀(dω(y))dν(y) = 0 by the hypothesis applied to the test form ω of step 3. (ii) The map v ↦ I(v) := ∫Dψ(y)[v]dν(y) is linear on ℝ^P: for each v, y ↦ Dψ(y)[v] is continuous (ψ is C^1) and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport ψ, hence is bounded and ν-integrable because ν is finite on compact sets; so I(v + v') = I(v) + I(v') and I(cv) = cI(v) (integral_add, integral_smul), and I(0) = 0. (iii) A linear functional vanishing on the generators v_α vanishes on their span (Submodule.span_induction), so I(v) = 0 for every v ∈ V.
6. (Proof of (b).) Let w ∈ V^⊥, α a d-covector and γ an n-covector with γ(u) = Σ_i (−1)^i⟨w, u_i⟩α(removeNth i u) for all u. By step 1(i), γ = w^♭∧α, so ζ₀(γ) = ⟨v_α, w⟩ = 0 because v_α ∈ V (Submodule.subset_span) and w ∈ V^⊥ (Submodule.inner_right_of_mem_orthogonal). ∎
proof_key_steps: w^♭∧α := d(⟨w,·⟩α)(0) has the stated alternating-sum formula (extderiv_smul) and is linear in w; let v_α be the Riesz representative of w ↦ ζ₀(w^♭∧α) and V := span{v_α}.

For ψ ∈ C_c^∞ the test form ψα has d(ψα)(y) = (∇ψ(y))^♭∧α, so ζ₀(d(ψα)(y)) = Dψ(y)[v_α] and the hypothesis gives ∫Dψ[v_α]dν = 0; by linearity of v ↦ ∫Dψ[v]dν (integrands continuous with compact support, ν finite on compacts) this extends to V.
For w ⊥ V and γ = w^♭∧α, ζ₀(γ) = ⟨v_α, w⟩ = 0.

Source: step 3 of the parent proof ("only coordinates inside V₀ matter": β = Σ_Iβ(e'_I)e'^I, and e'^I = ±e'^{i♭}∧e'^{I∖i} is killed by ζ₀ when I contains some i > r), for an arbitrary subspace V; the hypothesis is exactly the vanishing ζ₀(w^♭∧α) = 0 for w ⊥ V₀ used there. The parent's conclusion ζ₀(β) = Σ_{I⊆{1..r}}β(e'_I)ζ₀(e'^I) is rewritten as ζ(β) = ζ(β∘p_V) in step 6.
Notation: n = d + 1, r := dim V, p := p_V; tuples are indexed by Fin n = {0, …, d}; for an n-tuple u, removeNth a u deletes u_a; for j : Fin n → Fin P and a family e', e'_j := (e'_{j(0)}, …, e'_{j(d)}).
1. (Adapted orthonormal basis.) Choose an orthonormal basis e'_0, …, e'_{P−1} of ℝ^P such that e'_0, …, e'_{r−1} is an orthonormal basis of V and e'_r, …, e'_{P−1} an orthonormal basis of V^⊥ (ℝ^P = V ⊕ V^⊥ orthogonally; concatenate orthonormal bases of V and V^⊥). Then p e'_i = e'_i for i < r and p e'_i = 0 for i ≥ r.
2. (Dual n-covectors.) For a strictly increasing I = (i_0 < … < i_d) in {0, …, P−1} let e'^I(u) := det(⟨u_a, e'_{i_b}⟩)_{a,b ∈ Fin n}. Row a depends linearly on u_a and the determinant is multilinear and alternating in the rows, so e'^I is an n-covector (continuous by finite dimension). For j : Fin n → Fin P, e'^I(e'_j) = det(δ_{j(a), i_b})_{a,b}; this equals sign(π) if j = I∘π for a permutation π of Fin n (a permutation matrix), and 0 otherwise (if some j(a) ∉ {i_0, …, i_d}, row a is zero; if j is not injective, two rows coincide).
3. (Expansion.) Every n-covector β satisfies β = Σ_I β(e'_I)·e'^I (sum over strictly increasing I). Both sides are multilinear, so by expanding each argument u_a = Σ_m⟨u_a, e'_m⟩e'_m it suffices to compare their values on basis tuples e'_j, j : Fin n → Fin P. If j is not injective, both sides vanish (alternating maps on a tuple with a repeated entry; step 2). If j is injective, j = J∘π for a unique strictly increasing J and permutation π; by step 2 the right side equals β(e'_J)·sign(π), and the left side is β(e'_{J∘π}) = sign(π)·β(e'_J) because β is alternating.
4. (Index sets leaving V are killed.) Let I = (i_0 < … < i_d) with i_k ≥ r for some k. Laplace expansion of det(⟨u_a, e'_{i_b}⟩) along column k (Matrix.det_succ_column) gives e'^I(u) = Σ_a (−1)^{a+k}⟨u_a, e'_{i_k}⟩·det(⟨u_{a'}, e'_{i_{b'}}⟩)_{a'≠a, b'≠k} = Σ_a (−1)^a⟨e'_{i_k}, u_a⟩·α(removeNth a u), where α := (−1)^k·e'^{I∖i_k} is the d-covector built as in step 2 from the strictly increasing d-tuple I∖i_k (the minor with row a and column k deleted is the matrix of removeNth a u against I∖i_k). For d = 0, α is the constant 0-covector with value (−1)^k (the determinant of the empty matrix is 1). Hence γ := e'^I satisfies the formula of the hypothesis with w := e'_{i_k}, which lies in V^⊥ because i_k ≥ r; therefore ζ(e'^I) = 0.
5. (Consequence.) By step 3, linearity of ζ and step 4: ζ(β) = Σ_{I ⊆ {0..r−1}} β(e'_I)·ζ(e'^I) for every n-covector β, the sum running over strictly increasing I with all entries < r (an empty sum if r < n).
6. (Apply to β∘p.) β' := β∘p is an n-covector. For strictly increasing I with all entries < r, β'(e'_I) = β(p e'_{i_0}, …, p e'_{i_d}) = β(e'_I) by step 1. Applying step 5 to β' gives ζ(β∘p) = Σ_{I⊆{0..r−1}} β'(e'_I)ζ(e'^I) = Σ_{I⊆{0..r−1}} β(e'_I)ζ(e'^I) = ζ(β). ∎
Formalization notes (all reachable from GMT.Ch07.Submission): e'^I can be built as the ContinuousAlternatingMap whose underlying alternating map is Matrix.detRowAlternating.compLinearMap (LinearMap.pi fun b => innerₛₗ ℝ (e'_{i_b})) (row a = (⟨e'_{i_b}, u_a⟩)_b), continuity coming from Continuous.matrix_det / Continuous.matrixOf (fun_prop), packaged with ContinuousAlternatingMap.mk; Module.Basis.ext_alternating reduces the expansion of step 3 to basis tuples; ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_apply gives w^♭∧α = alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ w).smulRight α) directly; Matrix.det_permutation is not importable, use Matrix.det_permute or AlternatingMap.map_perm.
proof_key_steps: Take an orthonormal basis e' of ℝ^P whose first r vectors span V; every n-covector expands as β = Σ_Iβ(e'_I)e'^I with e'^I(u) = det(⟨u_a, e'_{i_b}⟩).
If I contains an index i_k ≥ r, Laplace expansion along column k writes e'^I = w^♭∧α with w = e'_{i_k} ∈ V^⊥, so ζ(e'^I) = 0.
Hence ζ(β) = Σ_{I⊆{0..r−1}}β(e'_I)ζ(e'^I); β∘p_V has the same coefficients on such I, so ζ(β∘p_V) = ζ(β).

subproblems.title: Translation invariance under V and growth O(Rⁿ) force dim V ≤ n
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, ν a Borel measure on ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace and C ∈ [0, ∞) (C : ℝ≥0∞, C ≠ ∞). Assume ν({x : v + x ∈ A}) = ν(A) for every v ∈ V and every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P, ν(B_R(0)) ≤ C·Rⁿ for every R > 0, and ν(B_1(0)) > 0 (open balls). Then dim V ≤ n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (C : ℝ≥0∞), C ≠ ∞ → (∀ v ∈ V, ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → ν ((fun x => v + x) ⁻¹' A) = ν A) → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ν (ball 0 R) ≤ C * ENNReal.ofReal (R ^ n)) → 0 < ν (ball 0 1) → Module.finrank ℝ V ≤ n
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof ("growth forces r ≤ n"), with ω_n replaced by an arbitrary finite constant C; there C = ω_n (hypothesis (2)) and ν(B_1(0)) > 0 is hypothesis (3) at r = 1.
1. Let r := dim V and m₀ := ν(B_1(0)). Then 0 < m₀ ≤ C·1 < ∞ (growth with R = 1). If r = 0 there is nothing to prove; assume r ≥ 1 and let e'_1, …, e'_r be an orthonormal basis of V.
2. (Equal mass of translated unit balls.) For u ∈ V we have −u ∈ V and {x : −u + x ∈ B_1(0)} = B_1(u), so ν(B_1(u)) = ν(B_1(0)) = m₀ by the invariance hypothesis (open balls are Borel).
3. (Packing.) Fix an integer M ≥ 1 and let Λ_M := {k ∈ ℤ^r : |k_j| ≤ M for all j}, a set with (2M+1)^r elements. For k ∈ Λ_M put u_k := 2Σ_j k_je'_j ∈ V. By orthonormality ‖u_k − u_l‖ = 2‖k − l‖_{ℓ²} ≥ 2 for k ≠ l, so the balls B_1(u_k), k ∈ Λ_M, are pairwise disjoint; and ‖u_k‖ = 2‖k‖_{ℓ²} ≤ 2M√r, so B_1(u_k) ⊆ B_{R_M}(0) with R_M := 2M√r + 1 ≤ 3M√r (as M√r ≥ 1).
4. (Counting.) By steps 2–3, additivity and monotonicity, and the growth hypothesis at R_M > 0: (2M+1)^r·m₀ = Σ_{k∈Λ_M}ν(B_1(u_k)) = ν(⋃_kB_1(u_k)) ≤ ν(B_{R_M}(0)) ≤ C·R_M^n ≤ C·(3√r)^n·M^n.
5. (Conclusion.) Suppose r > n. Since M^r ≤ (2M+1)^r, step 4 gives M^{r−n} ≤ C(3√r)^n/m₀ for every integer M ≥ 1. The right side is a finite real constant (C < ∞, m₀ > 0), while M^{r−n} → ∞ as M → ∞ — a contradiction. Hence r ≤ n. ∎
proof_key_steps: Translation invariance gives ν(B_1(u)) = ν(B_1(0)) = m₀ ∈ (0, ∞) for every u ∈ V.
The (2M+1)^r points 2Σk_je'_j (|k_j| ≤ M) of V have pairwise disjoint unit balls inside B_{3M√r}(0).
(2M+1)^r m₀ ≤ C(3M√r)^n for all M forces r ≤ n.

subproblems.title: Normalisation: a dual-norm-one n-vector that only sees an at most n-dimensional V is the unit n-vector of V
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, n := d+1, ζ₀ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n) and V ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace with dim V ≤ n and orthogonal projection p_V (V.starProjection). Assume |ζ₀(β)| ≤ |β| for every n-covector β, ζ₀(β₁) = 1 for some n-covector β₁ with |β₁| ≤ 1 (|·| = covectorEuclideanNorm), and ζ₀(β) = ζ₀(β∘p_V) for every n-covector β, where (β∘p_V)(u) := β(p_Vu_0, …, p_Vu_d). Then dim V = n, and there is an orthonormal family v = (v_0, …, v_d) in ℝ^P with span{v_0, …, v_d} = V and ζ₀(β) = β(v_0, …, v_d) for every n-covector β.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (ζ₀ : MultiVector P (d + 1)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V ≤ d + 1 → (∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1), |ζ₀ β| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm β) → (∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1), covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ 1 ∧ ζ₀ β = 1) → (∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1), ζ₀ β = ζ₀ (β.compContinuousLinearMap V.starProjection)) → Module.finrank ℝ V = d + 1 ∧ ∃ v : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ v ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) = V ∧ ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1), ζ₀ β = β v
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the end of step 3 ("as ζ₀(β₁) = 1 ≠ 0 … r ≥ n"), the last sentence of step 4 (ζ₀(β) = s·β(e'_1, …, e'_n)) and step 5 (normalisation) of the parent proof. Uses the siblings covector_eval_le = Fact (O1) (regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le: |α(τ)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α and orthonormal τ) and covector_norming = Fact (O2) (regcomp_exists_covector_eval_orthonormal_eq_one: for orthonormal τ there is β with |β| = 1 and β(τ) = 1).
Notation: n = d + 1, p := p_V, r := dim V ≤ n, β∘p := β.compContinuousLinearMap p.
1. (r = n.) Suppose r < n. For every n-covector β and every u, the n vectors p u_0, …, p u_d lie in V, whose dimension is r < n, so they are linearly dependent, and the alternating map β vanishes on them (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent). Thus β∘p = 0 and ζ₀(β) = ζ₀(β∘p) = ζ₀(0) = 0 for every β, contradicting ζ₀(β₁) = 1. Hence r = n.
2. (Frame.) As dim V = n, V has an orthonormal basis indexed by Fin n (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V reindexed along finrank ℝ V = n); let v = (v_0, …, v_d) be its image in ℝ^P. Then v is orthonormal in ℝ^P and span{v_0, …, v_d} = V.
3. (Top-degree forms on V.) Restricted to V, every n-covector γ gives an alternating n-form γ|_V on the n-dimensional space V; by uniqueness of top-degree alternating forms (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det with the basis v of V), γ|_V = γ(v)·det_v, where det_v is the determinant in the basis v. As p u_a ∈ V for every u, γ(p u_0, …, p u_d) = γ(v)·det_v(p u_0, …, p u_d) for all u. (Concretely p x = Σ_b⟨v_b, x⟩v_b and det_v(p u) = det(⟨v_b, u_a⟩)_{a,b}.)
4. (The constant s.) By covector_norming (applied to the orthonormal family v) there is an n-covector β₂ with |β₂| = 1 and β₂(v) = 1. By step 3 applied to β and to β₂, β(p u) = β(v)·det_v(p u) = β(v)·β₂(p u) for all u, i.e. β∘p = β(v)·(β₂∘p). Put s := ζ₀(β₂). Using the hypothesis twice and linearity of ζ₀: ζ₀(β) = ζ₀(β∘p) = β(v)·ζ₀(β₂∘p) = β(v)·ζ₀(β₂) = β(v)·s for every n-covector β. (This avoids constructing the covector β_v(u) = det(⟨v_b, u_a⟩) of the parent proof: β₂ plays its role, since β₂∘p = β_v.)
5. (|s| ≤ 1.) s = ζ₀(β₂), so |s| ≤ |β₂| = 1 by the hypothesis |ζ₀(β)| ≤ |β|.
6. (|s| ≥ 1.) By covector_eval_le, |β₁(v)| ≤ |β₁| ≤ 1. By step 4, 1 = ζ₀(β₁) = s·β₁(v), so 1 = |s|·|β₁(v)| ≤ |s|.
7. (Sign.) Hence |s| = 1, i.e. s = 1 or s = −1. If s = 1, ζ₀(β) = β(v) for every β. If s = −1, let v' := (−v_0, v_1, …, v_d) (Function.update v 0 (−v_0)): v' is orthonormal, span{v'} = span{v} = V, and β(v') = −β(v) by linearity of β in its first argument (MultilinearMap.map_update_smul / map_neg on β.toAlternatingMap), so ζ₀(β) = −β(v) = β(v') for every β.
8. (Conclusion.) dim V = n = d + 1, and the family v (if s = 1) or v' (if s = −1) is orthonormal, spans V, and satisfies ζ₀(β) = β(·) for every n-covector β. ∎
proof_key_steps: If dim V < n then β∘p_V = 0 for every β (linearly dependent arguments), so ζ₀ = 0, contradicting ζ₀(β₁) = 1; hence dim V = n.
For an orthonormal basis v of V and β₂ from (O2), uniqueness of top-degree forms on V gives β∘p_V = β(v)·(β₂∘p_V), so ζ₀(β) = s·β(v) with s = ζ₀(β₂), |s| ≤ |β₂| = 1.
(O1) with ζ₀(β₁) = 1 gives |s| ≥ 1, so s = ±1; if s = −1 flip v_0.

subproblems.title: Product structure ν = (Hⁿ⌞V) ⊗ σ of a locally finite measure invariant under translations by an n-dimensional subspace V
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace with dim V = n, and ν a Borel measure on ℝ^P with ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K and ν({x : v + x ∈ A}) = ν(A) for every v ∈ V and Borel A. Then there is a Borel measure σ on ℝ^P with σ(ℝ^P∖V^⊥) = 0 and σ(K) < ∞ for every compact K, such that ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V} σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]; lower Lebesgue integral over V), i.e. ν is the image of (Hⁿ⌞V) ⊗ σ under (t, y) ↦ t + y.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ν K < ∞) → (∀ v ∈ V, ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → ν ((fun x => v + x) ⁻¹' A) = ν A) → ∃ σ : Measure (Euclid P), σ (Vᗮ : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → σ K < ∞) ∧ ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → ν A = ∫⁻ t in (V : Set (Euclid P)), σ ((fun y => t + y) ⁻¹' A) ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 (V10, product structure) of the parent proof, for a general n-dimensional invariance subspace V (= V₀ there), with the measure σ of that step regarded as a measure on ℝ^P concentrated on V^⊥. Uses the sibling subspace_ball (accepted idtp_tdc_subspace_ball_measure): Hⁿ(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_nρⁿ for an n-dimensional subspace Q, y ∈ Q, ρ > 0, where ω_n = unitBallVolume n.
Notation: p := V.starProjection, q := V^⊥.starProjection, so y = p y + q y, p y ∈ V, q y ∈ V^⊥, ‖y‖² = ‖p y‖² + ‖q y‖², and for t ∈ V: p(t + y) = t + p y, q(t + y) = q y. ω_n = vol(B_1(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ) ∈ (0, ∞) (a nonempty bounded open set). A rectangle is a set p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(B) with A, B ⊆ ℝ^P Borel.
1. (Coordinates on V.) Let v_1, …, v_n be an orthonormal basis of V, L : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, L(x) := Σ_bx_bv_b (a linear isometry onto V) and π : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ, π(y) := (⟨v_b, y⟩)_b (continuous linear). Then L(π(y)) = p y, π(L x) = x, π(t + y) = π(t) + π(y), and ‖π(y)‖ = ‖p y‖. By Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, L_#vol = Hⁿ⌞(range L) = Hⁿ⌞V, i.e. vol(L⁻¹(A)) = Hⁿ(A ∩ V) for Borel A.
2. (Haar uniqueness for bounded B.) Fix a bounded Borel B ⊆ ℝ^P and let m_B := π_#(ν⌞q⁻¹(B)), a Borel measure on ℝⁿ with m_B(E) = ν(π⁻¹(E) ∩ q⁻¹(B)) for Borel E. (a) m_B is finite on compact sets: if E ⊆ B̄_R(0) and B ⊆ B̄_S(0), then π⁻¹(E) ∩ q⁻¹(B) ⊆ B̄_{R+S}(0), a compact set of finite ν-measure. (b) m_B is translation invariant: for x ∈ ℝⁿ and Borel E, π(L x + y) = x + π(y) and q(L x + y) = q y give {y : x + π(y) ∈ E, q y ∈ B} = {y : L x + y ∈ π⁻¹(E) ∩ q⁻¹(B)}; as L x ∈ V, the invariance of ν yields m_B({z : x + z ∈ E}) = ν(π⁻¹(E) ∩ q⁻¹(B)) = m_B(E). (c) By uniqueness of Haar measure (Measure.isAddLeftInvariant_eq_smul, Lebesgue measure being an additive Haar measure on ℝⁿ), m_B = κ_B·vol with κ_B = m_B.addHaarScalarFactor vol ∈ [0, ∞). Evaluating on the unit ball: κ_Bω_n = m_B(B_1(0)) = ν({y : ‖p y‖ < 1, q y ∈ B}).
3. (Definition of σ.) Let σ := ω_n⁻¹·q_#(ν⌞{y : ‖p y‖ < 1}), so σ(B) = ω_n⁻¹ν({y : ‖p y‖ < 1, q y ∈ B}) for Borel B. Then σ(ℝ^P∖V^⊥) = 0 because q y ∈ V^⊥ for every y; σ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ B̄_S(0), because {y : ‖p y‖ < 1, q y ∈ K} ⊆ B̄_{1+S}(0); and κ_B = σ(B) for bounded Borel B by step 2(c).
4. (Rectangle formula.) For Borel A and bounded Borel B: p⁻¹(A) = π⁻¹(L⁻¹(A)), so ν(p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(B)) = m_B(L⁻¹(A)) = σ(B)·vol(L⁻¹(A)) = σ(B)·Hⁿ(A ∩ V) by steps 1–3. For arbitrary Borel B apply this to B_j := B ∩ B_j(0), which increase to B, and pass to the limit by continuity from below on both sides (⨆_j(σ(B_j)·c) = (⨆_jσ(B_j))·c in [0, ∞], ENNReal.iSup_mul): ν(p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(B)) = σ(B)·Hⁿ(A ∩ V) for all Borel A, B.
5. (The measure λ.) σ is σ-finite (finite on compact sets, ℝ^P σ-compact), which is what Measure.prod_apply needs (SFinite σ); Hⁿ⌞V = L_#vol is σ-finite as well (Hⁿ(V ∩ B_j(0)) = ω_njⁿ < ∞ by subspace_ball). Let λ := s_#((Hⁿ⌞V) ⊗ σ) with s(t, y) := t + y (continuous). For Borel A, Measure.map_apply and Measure.prod_apply give λ(A) = ∫⁻σ({y : (t, y) ∈ s⁻¹(A)}) d(Hⁿ⌞V)(t) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t). Hence it suffices to prove ν = λ.
6. (Agreement on rectangles.) Let S = p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(B). For t ∈ V and y ∈ V^⊥, p(t + y) = t and q(t + y) = y; since σ is concentrated on V^⊥, σ({y : t + y ∈ S}) = σ({y ∈ V^⊥ : t ∈ A, y ∈ B}) = 1_A(t)·σ(B) for t ∈ V. Therefore λ(S) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}1_A(t)σ(B) dHⁿ(t) = σ(B)·Hⁿ(V ∩ A) = ν(S) by step 4.
7. (Generation.) Rectangles are Borel and form a π-system (p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(B) ∩ p⁻¹(A') ∩ q⁻¹(B') = p⁻¹(A ∩ A') ∩ q⁻¹(B ∩ B')). The σ-algebra 𝒢 they generate contains p⁻¹(A) = p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(ℝ^P) and q⁻¹(B), so p and q are 𝒢-measurable, hence so is y ↦ p y + q y = y (Measurable.add into the second-countable ℝ^P); thus every Borel set belongs to 𝒢, and 𝒢 is the Borel σ-algebra.
8. (Conclusion.) The rectangles S_j := p⁻¹(B_j(0)) ∩ q⁻¹(B_j(0)) (j ∈ ℕ) cover ℝ^P and ν(S_j) ≤ ν(B̄_{2j}(0)) < ∞. By steps 6–7 and Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion, ν = λ, i.e. ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) for every Borel A; with step 3 this is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: For bounded Borel B, E ↦ ν(π⁻¹(E) ∩ q⁻¹(B)) is a translation-invariant locally finite measure on ℝⁿ ≅ V, so by Haar uniqueness it is σ(B)·vol with σ(B) = ω_n⁻¹ν({‖p y‖ < 1, q y ∈ B}).
Hence ν(p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(B)) = σ(B)Hⁿ(A ∩ V) for all Borel A, B (bounded B first, then monotone limits); σ is concentrated on V^⊥ and finite on compact sets.
λ := ((Hⁿ⌞V) ⊗ σ) pushed forward by addition agrees with ν on the generating π-system of rectangles, finite on a countable cover, so ν = λ, which is the integral formula.

subproblems.title: The lower density bound makes the transversal measure purely atomic with atoms ≥ c: ν is a countable sum of weighted parallel planes
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, c > 0, V ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace with dim V = n, σ a Borel measure on ℝ^P with σ(ℝ^P∖V^⊥) = 0 and σ(K) < ∞ for compact K, and ν a Borel measure on ℝ^P with ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) for every Borel A (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Assume ofReal c ≤ liminf_{r→0+} ν(B_r(y))/(ω_n·rⁿ) for ν-a.e. y (ω_n = unitBallVolume n). Then there is a countable set Z ⊆ V^⊥ with σ({w}) ≥ ofReal c for every w ∈ Z and ν = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V} (Measure.sum indexed by Z).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 ("σ is purely atomic with atoms ≥ c") and the first sentence of step 8 ("ν = Σ_iα_iHⁿ⌞(V₀ + w_i) (step 6)") of the parent proof. Uses the sibling subspace_ball (accepted idtp_tdc_subspace_ball_measure): Hⁿ(V ∩ B_ρ(u)) = ω_nρⁿ for u ∈ V, ρ > 0.
Notation: p, q the orthogonal projections onto V and V^⊥ (y = p y + q y); ω_n ∈ (0, ∞); (D) is the hypothesis ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) for Borel A. For t ∈ V, {y : t + y ∈ B_r(x)} = B_r(x − t).
1. (Upper bound.) Let x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0. For t ∈ V and z ∈ V^⊥: z − (x − t) = (z − q x) + (t − p x) with z − q x ∈ V^⊥ and t − p x ∈ V, so ‖z − (x − t)‖² = ‖z − q x‖² + ‖t − p x‖². Hence B_r(x − t) ∩ V^⊥ ⊆ B_r(q x), and B_r(x − t) ∩ V^⊥ = ∅ unless ‖t − p x‖ < r. Since σ is concentrated on V^⊥, σ(B_r(x − t)) ≤ 1_{B_r(p x)}(t)·σ(B_r(q x)) for t ∈ V. Integrating over V and using (D) with A = B_r(x): ν(B_r(x)) ≤ σ(B_r(q x))·Hⁿ(V ∩ B_r(p x)) = ω_nrⁿσ(B_r(q x)) (subspace_ball; p x ∈ V).
2. (Density bound.) As ω_nrⁿ ∈ (0, ∞) for r > 0, step 1 gives ν(B_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≤ σ(B_r(q x)) for every r > 0. As r ↓ 0, σ(B_r(q x)) tends to σ({q x}): r ↦ B_r(q x) is monotone, ⋂_{r>0}B_r(q x) = {q x}, and σ(B_1(q x)) ≤ σ(B̄_1(q x)) < ∞ (continuity from above along 𝓝[>] 0, tendsto_measure_biInter_gt; alternatively bound the liminf by σ(B_{1/(k+1)}(q x)) for every k and use tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop). Hence liminf_{r→0+}ν(B_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≤ σ({q x}), and by hypothesis ofReal c ≤ σ({q x}) for ν-a.e. x.
3. (The atoms.) Let Z := {w ∈ V^⊥ : ofReal c ≤ σ({w})}. For every j ∈ ℕ, Z ∩ B̄_j(0) is finite: for every finite F ⊆ Z ∩ B̄_j(0), #F·ofReal c ≤ Σ_{w∈F}σ({w}) = σ(F) ≤ σ(B̄_j(0)) < ∞, so #F ≤ σ(B̄_j(0))/ofReal c, a bound independent of F. Hence Z = ⋃_j(Z ∩ B̄_j(0)) is countable, and in particular Borel (Set.Countable.measurableSet).
4. (σ lives on Z.) E := q⁻¹(ℝ^P∖Z) is Borel. For ν-a.e. x, q x ∈ V^⊥ and ofReal c ≤ σ({q x}) (step 2), i.e. q x ∈ Z; so ν(E) = 0. For t ∈ V, q(t + y) = q y, hence {y : t + y ∈ E} = E, and (D) gives 0 = ν(E) = σ(E)·Hⁿ(V). Since Hⁿ(V) ≥ Hⁿ(V ∩ B_1(0)) = ω_n > 0 (subspace_ball), σ(E) = 0. As q z = z for z ∈ V^⊥, (ℝ^P∖Z) ∩ V^⊥ ⊆ E, so σ(ℝ^P∖Z) ≤ σ(E) + σ(ℝ^P∖V^⊥) = 0.
5. (σ is a sum of point masses.) For Borel B, B ∩ Z is countable, so by step 4 and countable additivity σ(B) = σ(B ∩ Z) = Σ_{w∈B∩Z}σ({w}) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·δ_w(B).
6. (ν is a sum of planes.) Let A be Borel. By (D) and step 5 (applied to B = {y : t + y ∈ A}), ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})1_A(t + w) dHⁿ(t) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})∫⁻_{t∈V}1_A(t + w) dHⁿ(t) (lintegral_tsum over the countable index set Z; each t ↦ 1_A(t + w) is Borel) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·Hⁿ(V ∩ (A − w)), where A − w := {t : t + w ∈ A}. The translation t ↦ t + w is an isometry of ℝ^P mapping V ∩ (A − w) onto A ∩ {y : y − w ∈ V}, and Hⁿ is invariant under isometries (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), so Hⁿ(V ∩ (A − w)) = Hⁿ(A ∩ {y : y − w ∈ V}) = (Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V})(A) ({y : y − w ∈ V} is closed and A Borel, Measure.restrict_apply). Therefore ν(A) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·(Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V})(A) = (Measure.sum_{w∈Z}σ({w})•Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V})(A) (Measure.sum_apply) for every Borel A, and the two measures are equal (Measure.ext).
7. (Conclusion.) Z is countable, Z ⊆ V^⊥ and ofReal c ≤ σ({w}) for w ∈ Z by construction, and step 6 is the required identity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Pythagoras transversally to V gives ν(B_r(x)) ≤ ω_nrⁿσ(B_r(q x)), so the lower density bound yields σ({q x}) ≥ c for ν-a.e. x.
Z := {w ∈ V^⊥ : σ({w}) ≥ c} is locally finite hence countable; ν(q⁻¹(Zᶜ)) = 0 and the product formula give σ(Zᶜ) = 0, so σ = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})δ_w.
Inserting σ = Σσ({w})δ_w in the product formula and using translation invariance of Hⁿ gives ν = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V}.

subproblems.title: Growth and positivity make a sum of weighted parallel planes finite, with total weight ≤ 1 and one plane through 0
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, c > 0, V ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace with dim V = n, Z ⊆ V^⊥ any set and a : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] with a(w) ≥ ofReal c for every w ∈ Z, and let ν = Σ_{w∈Z}a(w)·Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V} (Measure.sum indexed by Z; Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Assume ν(B_R(0)) ≤ ω_nRⁿ for all R > 0 (ω_n = unitBallVolume n) and ν(B_r(0)) > 0 for all r > 0. Then there are N ∈ ℕ, pairwise distinct w_1, …, w_N ∈ V^⊥ and reals α_1, …, α_N ≥ c with Σ_iα_i ≤ 1, such that some w_i = 0 and ν = Σ_{i=1}^{N}ofReal(α_i)·Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w_i ∈ V}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (Z : Set (Euclid P)) (a : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → Module.finrank ℝ V = n → Z ⊆ (Vᗮ : Set (Euclid P)) → (∀ w ∈ Z, ENNReal.ofReal c ≤ a w) → ν = Measure.sum (fun w : Z => a w • (μHE[n]).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - w ∈ V}) → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ν (ball 0 R) ≤ unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (R ^ n)) → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → 0 < ν (ball 0 r)) → ∃ (N : ℕ) (w : Fin N → Euclid P) (α : Fin N → ℝ), Injective w ∧ (∀ i, w i ∈ Vᗮ) ∧ (∀ i, c ≤ α i) ∧ ∑ i, α i ≤ 1 ∧ (∃ i, w i = 0) ∧ ν = ∑ i, ENNReal.ofReal (α i) • (μHE[n]).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - w i ∈ V}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 8 ("finitely many planes with Σα_i ≤ 1"), 9 ("some w_i = 0") and 10 (the required form) of the parent proof. Uses the sibling subspace_ball (accepted idtp_tdc_subspace_ball_measure): Hⁿ(V ∩ B_ρ(0)) = ω_nρⁿ for ρ > 0.
Notation: Π_w := {y : y − w ∈ V} (a closed, hence Borel, translate of V); ω_n ∈ (0, ∞).
1. (A plane in a ball.) Let w ∈ V^⊥ and R > 0. For t ∈ V, ‖t + w‖² = ‖t‖² + ‖w‖² (t ⊥ w). Hence, if ‖w‖ < R and ρ := (R² − ‖w‖²)^{1/2} > 0, the isometry t ↦ t + w maps V ∩ B_ρ(0) onto Π_w ∩ B_R(0); and if ‖w‖ ≥ R, Π_w ∩ B_R(0) = ∅. By isometry invariance of Hⁿ (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) and subspace_ball: Hⁿ(Π_w ∩ B_R(0)) = ω_n(R² − ‖w‖²)^{n/2} = ω_nρⁿ if ‖w‖ < R, and = 0 if ‖w‖ ≥ R.
2. (Evaluating ν.) For Borel B, ν(B) = Σ_{w∈Z}a(w)·Hⁿ(B ∩ Π_w) (Measure.sum_apply, Measure.smul_apply, Measure.restrict_apply).
3. (Finite subfamilies.) Let F ⊆ Z be finite and R > max_{w∈F}‖w‖ (any R > 0 if F = ∅). By steps 1–2 and the growth hypothesis, Σ_{w∈F}a(w)ω_n(R² − ‖w‖²)^{n/2} ≤ ν(B_R(0)) ≤ ω_nRⁿ; dividing by ω_nRⁿ ∈ (0, ∞), Σ_{w∈F}a(w)(1 − ‖w‖²/R²)^{n/2} ≤ 1. Given ε ∈ (0, 1), choose R so large that (1 − ‖w‖²/R²)^{n/2} ≥ 1 − ε for all w ∈ F (finitely many conditions); then (1 − ε)Σ_{w∈F}a(w) ≤ 1. As ε is arbitrary, Σ_{w∈F}a(w) ≤ 1 (in particular a(w) < ∞ for w ∈ F; the inequality is read in [0, ∞]).
4. (Finiteness.) For every finite F ⊆ Z, #F·c ≤ Σ_{w∈F}a(w) ≤ 1, so #F ≤ 1/c. A set all of whose finite subsets have at most 1/c elements is finite, so Z is finite; with F = Z, Σ_{w∈Z}a(w) ≤ 1, hence ofReal c ≤ a(w) ≤ 1 for w ∈ Z.
5. (Enumeration.) Let N := #Z and e : Fin N ≃ Z (Set.Finite.fintype, Fintype.equivFin); put w_i := e(i) ∈ ℝ^P (pairwise distinct since e is injective; w_i ∈ Z ⊆ V^⊥) and α_i := (a(w_i)).toReal. As a(w_i) ∈ [ofReal c, 1], ofReal(α_i) = a(w_i), α_i ≥ c (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal) and Σ_iα_i = (Σ_ia(w_i)).toReal ≤ 1. A Measure.sum over the finite index set Z is the finite sum, reindexed along e, so ν = Σ_{i<N}ofReal(α_i)·Hⁿ⌞Π_{w_i}.
6. (Some w_i = 0.) Suppose w_i ≠ 0 for every i. If N = 0 then ν = 0, contradicting ν(B_1(0)) > 0. Otherwise r := min_i‖w_i‖ > 0; by step 1 (‖w_i‖ ≥ r) Hⁿ(Π_{w_i} ∩ B_r(0)) = 0 for every i, so ν(B_r(0)) = 0 by step 2, contradicting ν(B_r(0)) > 0. Hence w_i = 0 for some i. (This is the parent's argument: 0 ∈ spt ν = ⋃_iΠ_{w_i}, and 0 ∈ Π_{w_i} means w_i ∈ V ∩ V^⊥ = {0}.)
7. (Conclusion.) N, (w_i) and (α_i) satisfy: w injective, w_i ∈ V^⊥, α_i ≥ c, Σ_iα_i ≤ 1, some w_i = 0, and ν = Σ_iofReal(α_i)·Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w_i ∈ V}. ∎
proof_key_steps: For w ⊥ V, Hⁿ({y : y − w ∈ V} ∩ B_R(0)) = ω_n(R² − ‖w‖²)_+^{n/2} by Pythagoras, isometry invariance and subspace_ball.
The growth bound gives Σ_{w∈F}a(w)(1 − ‖w‖²/R²)^{n/2} ≤ 1 for finite F ⊆ Z; letting R → ∞, Σ_Fa(w) ≤ 1, so #Z ≤ 1/c and Σ_Za(w) ≤ 1.
Enumerate Z as w_1, …, w_N with α_i = a(w_i).toReal; positivity of ν(B_r(0)) for all r > 0 forces some w_i = 0.
